_note: A sample data dictionary for the Data Catalog's Upload schema or dictionary button.
Unknown top-level keys are ignored by the reader, so this note travels with the file.
Upload it against the CAPEX dataset, source bigquery:northline_epbcs, dataset plan.
It does two things on purpose, one per table:
plan_scenario_dim     — already in the project. Its 7 columns are catalogued but have no
dictionary, so today they are SYNTHESISED. Applying replaces them
with these, and the count stays 7 — the preview reads 7 -> 7.
plan_capital_gate_log — NOT in the project. A table this file declares has to carry a label
and a grain, because validateDb requires both and neither can be
invented; both are below. Its rows stay uncounted, not 0.
What to look for after applying:
· every column's derivation reads 'declared in <this filename>'
· null%, distinct and the classifier score are all '—'. A dictionary states what a column
means and samples nothing, so there is no figure to print and none is invented.
· a column with no class takes one from its type: NUMERIC -> measure, DATE -> date,
BOOL -> flag, STRING -> text. Nothing infers 'identifier' from a name ending in _id.
· gate_notes is a bare string with no type at all, so its type prints '—' and its
description status is 'needs review' — nobody has said what it means.
· a forced profiling run starts on both tables and the Catalog switches to Profiling jobs.
The preview writes nothing. It also warns if a Data Modeling declaration reads a column this
file does not name — neither table below is one anything has declarations on.

columns.description: The Scenario member key, as the cube stores it. Joins to plan_version_master.scenario.
What the scenario is called on screen — Budget, Actual, Forecast.
Whether the member holds a plan, a recorded actual, or a forecast vintage.
The default version this scenario resolves to when a form does not name one. No class stated, so it is read from the type.
Whether the scenario is open for input. Derived class: flag.
First period the scenario accepts data for. Derived class: date.
Who owns the scenario. Marked PII, so it answers the PII chip.

tables.label: Capital gate decisions
tables.grain: one row per project and gate decision

columns.description: The project the decision was made against. Declared as an identifier here, which is what lets the Data Modeling tab suggest the join.
Which gate in the stage sequence. Derived class: measure.
When the gate was decided. Derived class: date.
What the gate released, in dollars.
